chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu al-Abbas, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man leading the woman in prayer in his house, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, she should stand behind him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman praying behind a man in his house?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the domestic arrangement of *imamate*, confirming that a woman standing behind a man in prayer is legally valid (*sahih*). This ruling underscores the flexibility of private family prayer structures while maintaining the hierarchical order of leadership, distinguishing it from congregational mosque prayers where spatial arrangements may differ. It serves as a foundational text for Shia jurisprudence regarding household worship dynamics.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Al Abbas who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man leading the woman (in Salāt) in his house. So heasws said: ‘Yes, she should be standing behind him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan from abu al-‘Abbas who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who leads the woman in his house in Salah (prayer). He (the Imam) said, ’Yes, he can do so and she stands behind him.”’
